title: Toroidal 3D tic-tac-toe
words: Four-in-a-row on a 4 × 4 × 4 cube where every face wraps around. Who wins?
math: Solve the positional game on $\mathbb{Z}_4^3$ whose winning sets are all lines $\{x+td: t\in\mathbb{Z}_4\}$.

title: Forced SQG blow-up
words: Copy the 2026 forced Navier–Stokes blow-up for the surface quasi-geostrophic equation.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ such that forced SQG on $\mathbb{R}^2$ from rest blows up in finite time.

title: Smallest force for blow-up
words: How weak can the push be and still make viscous fluid blow up?
math: Find the optimal exponent $a$ with $\inf\{\|f\|_{L^\infty}: \text{NS from rest blows up}\}\asymp \nu^{a}$.

title: Exotic shuffles
words: For which deck sizes do the three-pile shuffles generate every possible arrangement?
math: Determine all $n$ for which the six 3-pile shuffles generate $S_{3n}$ or $A_{3n}$.

title: 3-SAT at density 4
words: Give a fast algorithm that solves almost all random 3-SAT puzzles up to clause density 4.
math: Give a polynomial-time algorithm finding satisfying assignments of random 3-SAT with density $4.0$ with probability $1-o(1)$.

title: 7×7 Othello
words: Who wins Othello on an odd 7×7 board with a fixed off-centre start?
math: Strongly solve Othello on a $7\times7$ board from the standard initial cross shifted to the corner-adjacent center.

title: Gerver and π
words: Show the sofa constant has no algebraic relation with π and e.
math: Prove $\mu_G,\pi,e$ are algebraically independent.

title: Seven-free primes are equidistributed in APs
words: Show seven-free primes are evenly spread among residue classes, with power-saving error for huge moduli.
math: Prove a Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem for 7-free primes with level of distribution $1/2+\delta$, $\delta>0$.

title: Two runners on a torus
words: Two runners move on a doughnut-shaped track with whole-number velocities. Show they eventually both get far from the start point.
math: For linearly independent $v_1,v_2\in\mathbb{Z}^2$, prove $\exists t:\ \|tv_i\|_{\mathbb{T}^2,\infty}\ge 1/3$ for $i=1,2$.

title: Polyhedral sofa
words: The best 3D sofa is curved. What is the best one with at most 12 flat corners?
math: Maximize volume over convex polyhedra with $\le12$ vertices admissible in the $1\times1$ square corridor.

title: Smallest-factor Collatz for all n
words: Prove every start reaches 1 under the smallest-odd-factor Collatz map.
math: Prove $g^k(n)=1$ for some $k$, for every $n\ge1$.

title: Closed-form Euler blow-up
words: Give smooth starting data for frictionless 3D fluid, written as an explicit formula, that blows up.
math: Find closed-form smooth finite-energy $u_0$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose unforced Euler solution blows up in finite time.

title: Shuffle cryptosystem
words: A cipher applies a secret sequence of three-pile shuffles. Show breaking it is as hard as a known problem.
math: Prove recovering a word of length $\ell$ in the six 3-pile shuffles from its permutation is NP-hard.

title: Hat Ising critical exponents in 3D layers
words: Find the exact critical exponents of the Ising model on layered hat tilings.
math: Compute $\nu$ and $\eta$ exactly for the Ising model on $\text{hat}\times\mathbb{Z}$.

title: Hat Ising bounds
words: Pin down the critical temperature of magnets on a hat tiling to within one percent.
math: Prove two-sided bounds on $T_c$ for the hat-graph Ising model with ratio $\le1.01$.

title: Prime Nim with two piles
words: Give an exact rule for who wins two-pile Prime Nim (remove a prime from one pile).
math: Characterize $\{(a,b): G(a)\oplus G(b)=0\}$ via a formula for the Grundy function $G$ of Prime Nim.

title: Random nonograms
words: Draw a random 20 × 20 black-and-white picture. How likely is its number clues to have only one solution?
math: For a uniform random $20\times20$ binary image, compute $\Pr(\text{its row/column clues determine it})$ to two decimals.

title: Optimal origami for every tree
words: For every stick-figure design, find the smallest square sheet that folds into it.
math: Give a polynomial-time algorithm computing the minimal square paper for a uniaxial base of any metric tree, with proof of optimality.

title: Emirps, almost
words: Show infinitely many primes have a reversal with at most three prime factors.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: \Omega(\operatorname{rev}(p))\le3\}\to\infty$.

title: Hat dimer heights
words: Random pairings of neighbouring hat tiles have a "height" landscape. Show it looks like the standard random surface at large scales.
math: Prove the height function of uniform dimer covers of growing hat patches converges to a multiple of the Gaussian free field, and compute the multiple.

title: Keller maps are invertible over Q in dimension 3, degree ≤ 4
words: Show no Jacobian-conjecture counterexample exists in 3D up to degree 4 with rational coefficients.
math: Prove every Keller map $F\in\mathbb{Q}[x,y,z]^3$ with $\deg F\le4$ is invertible.

title: Seven-free primes in short intervals
words: Show seven-free primes appear in every reasonably short interval.
math: Prove $[x,x+x^{0.6}]$ contains a prime with no digit 7 for all large $x$.

title: Keller maps in dimension 3 of degree 5
words: Show no Jacobian-conjecture counterexample exists in 3D with degree exactly 5 and rational coefficients.
math: Prove every Keller map $F\in\mathbb{Q}[x,y,z]^3$ with $\deg F=5$ is invertible.

title: Alternating prime residues
words: Find ten consecutive primes whose remainders mod 4 alternate 1, 3, 1, 3, …, and infinitely many such runs.
math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $p_{n+i}\equiv 2+(-1)^{i}\pmod 4$ for $0\le i<10$.

title: Polykite growth is irrational
words: Show the growth rate of polykite counts is an irrational number.
math: Prove $\lambda=\lim k_n^{1/n}$ for polykites is irrational.

title: Prime necklaces for all n
words: Arrange 1 to 2n in a circle so every two neighbours sum to a prime, and so do every two numbers three apart.
math: Prove for all large $n$ a cyclic arrangement of $[2n]$ with $\pi_i+\pi_{i+1}$ and $\pi_i+\pi_{i+3}$ prime for all $i$.

title: Counting 16 × 16 Sudoku
words: Count the essentially different 16 × 16 Sudoku grids, ignoring symmetries, to three significant figures.
math: Determine the automorphism group $\Gamma$ of the $16\times16$ Sudoku constraint structure and estimate $|\text{grids}/\Gamma|$ to 3 significant figures.

title: Three colors for cube sums
words: Can the positive integers be 3-colored so no two numbers of the same color add to a cube? Settle it.
math: Decide whether $\chi(C_\infty)\le3$, where $a\sim b$ iff $a+b$ is a perfect cube.

title: Quasi-RH in Lean
words: Turn the 2026 AI proof of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis into a full computer-checked proof.
math: Formalize in Lean 4 that $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\Re s>7/8$.

title: Prime-speed lonely runners
words: Prove the lonely runner conjecture when every speed is a prime number.
math: For distinct primes $p_1,\dots,p_n$, prove $\sup_t\min_i\|tp_i\|\ge\frac1{n+1}$.

title: Hadwiger's true constant
words: If graphs needing many colors need not contain a full complete-graph minor, find how large a complete minor they must contain.
math: Find $c^*=\liminf_{t}\min\{h(G)/t:\chi(G)\ge t\}$, where $h$ is the Hadwiger number.

title: Distinct prime sums
words: Arrange 1 to N in a circle so neighbouring sums are all different primes.
math: Prove for all large even $N$ there is a Hamiltonian cycle in the prime-sum graph on $[N]$ with pairwise distinct adjacent sums.

title: Hyperoperation fixed points
words: In any natural real-rank hyperoperation family, show the rank at which 2 ∘ 2 stops being 4 is not a whole number.
math: For the unique analytic family $a[s]b$ satisfying the recursion and log-convexity in $s$, prove $\{s: 2[s]2=4\}$ is exactly $[1,\infty)\cap$ an explicit closed set and determine whether it is an interval.

title: 7n+1 almost always
words: The largest-factor map with 7n + 1 should bring almost every start down to small numbers.
math: For $f_7(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(7n+1)$ (odd), prove $\{n: \exists k,\ f_7^k(n)<n\}$ has density 1.

title: Hex on hat boards, large
words: Solve Hex on hat-tiled boards of side 9.
math: Determine the winner of Hex on the hat-tiled rhombus board of side 9, with an explicit strategy.

title: Sudoku entropy
words: Show the number of complete Sudoku grids grows at a precise rate, and find that rate.
math: Prove $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log S_n}{n^4\log n}$ exists, where $S_n$ counts valid $n^2\times n^2$ grids, and compute it.

title: Hat dimers
words: Cover a hat tiling with dominoes joining neighbouring tiles. Count the coverings exactly per tile.
math: Compute the dimer entropy per vertex of the hat adjacency graph in closed form.

title: Gap patterns mod 4
words: Show the pattern "gap divisible by 4, then gap not divisible by 4" happens infinitely often among consecutive primes.
math: Prove $p_{n+1}-p_n\equiv0\pmod4$ and $p_n-p_{n-1}\equiv2\pmod4$ for infinitely many $n$.

title: Kakeya for hats
words: What is the smallest region in which you can rotate a hat tile through every orientation?
math: Determine $\inf$ area of sets containing a translate of every rotation of the hat polygon.

title: Convex hyperbolic monotile
words: Find a single convex tile that covers the hyperbolic plane but never in a repeating way.
math: Find a convex polygon $P\subset\mathbb{H}^2$ that tiles $\mathbb{H}^2$ and admits no tiling with a cocompact symmetry group.

title: Formalize the sofa
words: Turn Baek's proof that Gerver's sofa is optimal into a computer-checked proof.
math: Formalize in Lean 4 the statement and proof that the moving sofa constant equals the area of Gerver's sofa.

title: Square-sum graph is a minor of every large prime-sum graph
words: Show every square-sum graph sits inside a large enough prime-sum graph as a minor.
math: Prove for every $N$ there is $M$ such that $S_N$ is a minor of the prime-sum graph on $[M]$, with $M\le N^{C}$.

title: Sofa with a pillar
words: A thin pillar stands in the corner of the hallway. Find the best sofa that gets around it.
math: Determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor with a point obstacle at $(1/2,1/2)$ from the outer corner.

title: Small Keller maps in 3D
words: The 2026 counterexamples to the Jacobian conjecture have fairly high degree. Is there one of degree 5 or less?
math: Decide whether some $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with $\deg F\le5$ and $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ has no polynomial inverse.

title: Sudoku entropy bounds
words: Count how many complete Sudoku grids of size n² × n² exist, on a log scale. Pin the growth constant between 1 and 2.
math: Let $S_n$ be the number of valid $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku grids. Show $1\le \liminf \frac{\log S_n}{n^4\log n}\le \limsup \frac{\log S_n}{n^4\log n}\le 2$.

title: Formalize 3D Kakeya
words: Turn the 2025 proof of the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture into a compact computer-checked proof.
math: Produce a Lean 4 formalization of the Wang–Zahl theorem ($\dim_H K=3$ for Kakeya $K\subset\mathbb{R}^3$) in under 50,000 lines beyond Mathlib.

title: Unique Yang–Mills
words: Show the 2026 Yang–Mills theory does not depend on how it was built.
math: Prove the 2026 construction of 4D pure Yang–Mills is independent of the regularization and limit procedure.

title: SOF Collatz with 5n + 1
words: Use the smallest odd factor of 5n + 1 instead of 3n + 1. Show every start ends in a loop.
math: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto n/2$ (even), $\mathrm{spf}_{\text{odd}}(5n+1)$ (odd) is eventually periodic.

title: Spectre diffraction is pure point
words: Shine X-rays through a spectre tiling. Show the pattern has only sharp spots, no haze.
math: Prove the diffraction measure of the spectre tiling (unit point masses at tile centers) is pure point.

title: Three colors for square sums
words: Join two numbers when they add up to a perfect square. Find the first N where coloring 1 to N this way needs four colors.
math: Let $S_N$ have vertices $\{1,\dots,N\}$ and edges $\{a,b\}$ with $a+b$ a square. Find the least $N$ with $\chi(S_N)\ge4$.

title: Prime Nim complexity
words: Decide exactly how hard it is to tell if a Prime Nim pile is losing: show it can't be done fast without unproven assumptions.
math: Prove, unconditionally, that deciding $G(n)=0$ in Prime Nim requires time $(\log n)^{\omega(1)}$.

title: Fewest KenKen cages
words: What is the fewest cages for a uniquely solvable 6 × 6 KenKen puzzle?
math: Minimize the number of cages in a $6\times6$ KenKen (cage targets with $+,-,\times,\div$) having a unique Latin-square solution.

title: Hardest Rush Hour
words: Find the 7 × 7 Rush Hour traffic-jam puzzle that takes the most moves to solve.
math: Over all solvable $7\times7$ Rush Hour configurations, determine $\max$ of the minimum solution length, with a certificate.

title: Hat drum's first mode
words: Strike a hat-shaped drum. Show its lowest tone vibrates with a single peak.
math: Prove the first Dirichlet eigenfunction of the hat polygon has exactly one interior critical point.

title: Emirp asymptotic
words: Count emirps up to x to leading order.
math: Prove the number of $d$-digit emirps is $\sim c_d\,10^d/d^2$ with explicit $c_d$.

title: Sudoku completions are log-normal
words: Erase half a random Sudoku. The number of ways to refill it should follow a log-normal law.
math: For a random $9\times9$ grid with a uniformly random half of cells erased, prove $\log(\#\text{completions})$ is asymptotically normal under the natural $n^2\times n^2$ scaling.

title: LF-Collatz stopping time distribution
words: Find the exact distribution of how long the largest-factor Collatz map takes to settle.
math: Prove $T_f(n)/\log n$ converges in distribution on $[1,x]$ and identify the limit law.

title: Random Wang tiles
words: Pick n random tile types with colored edges. How likely are they to tile the plane?
math: For $n$ Wang tiles with edge colours i.i.d. uniform in $[c]$, find the asymptotics of $\Pr(\text{tiles }\mathbb{Z}^2)$ as $n\to\infty$.

title: Primes avoiding two digits
words: Show infinitely many primes avoid both the digits 3 and 7.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: \text{no digit }3\text{ or }7\}\sim c\,x^{\log 8/\log 10}/\log x$.

title: Mod-3 Collatz in every base
words: Generalize the mod-3 map to every base b. Show almost every start escapes, and find every loop, for all b at once.
math: For each $b\ge3$ define $h_b(n)=n/b$ if $b\mid n$, else $(b-1)n+(n\bmod b)$; prove that for every $b\ge3$ the set of $n$ with $h_b^k(n)\to\infty$ has density 1, and determine all cycles.

title: Prime Nim Grundy values are unbounded in density
words: Show each Grundy value of Prime Nim appears with a precise positive density, and compute them all.
math: Prove $d_k=\lim\frac1x\#\{n\le x: G(n)=k\}$ exists for every $k$ and give a formula.

title: Wind-driven fire in 3D
words: In 3D, fire spreads in five of six directions because of wind. How many firefighters per turn are needed?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^3$ with spread to all neighbours except $-e_1$, find the least per-turn budget containing a single fire.

title: Glueballs
words: Show the 2026 rigorous Yang–Mills theory contains a particle: an isolated energy level above the vacuum.
math: Prove the Hamiltonian of the 2026 pure Yang–Mills construction has an isolated eigenvalue in $(0,\infty)$.

title: Lean tactic termination
words: Show it is impossible to predict whether a simple rewriting tactic stops, for a natural class of rule sets.
math: Prove termination of Lean's `simp` on a given finite set of rewrite rules is undecidable for rule sets drawn from a fixed signature of size 3.

title: Cube-sum Hamiltonian cycles
words: Arrange 1 to N in a circle so neighbours add to perfect cubes, for all large N.
math: Prove $C_N$ is Hamiltonian for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Exact Wang busy beaver W(6)
words: Find the sixth value of the Wang-tile busy beaver.
math: Determine $W(6)$.

title: Voice-leading diameter in 19-tone
words: Find the farthest apart two 4-note chords can be in 19-tone tuning, when each move nudges one note by one step.
math: Determine the diameter of the voice-leading graph on 4-subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_{19}$ under single-semitone moves, with closed form in general $\mathbb{Z}_n$.

title: Prime Nim is not automatic
words: No finite machine reading digits can recognize Prime Nim losing positions.
math: Prove the P-position set is not $k$-automatic for any base $k\ge2$.

title: Coprime runners, three at a time
words: Three runners with pairwise coprime speeds lap a track; a stationary watcher eventually gets lonely. How much lonelier than the conjecture guarantees?
math: For pairwise coprime $v_1,v_2,v_3$, find the largest $c$ with $\sup_t \min_i \|tv_i\|\ge \tfrac14 + c$ for all such triples.

title: Graceful caterpillar unions
words: Show any number of copies of the same caterpillar can be labeled with distinct edge differences.
math: Prove $kT$ ($k$ disjoint copies of a caterpillar $T$) admits the graceful-forest labeling for all $k$.

title: Rounded corners
words: The inside corner of the hallway is rounded. Find the best sofa for every rounding radius.
math: For each $\rho\ge0$, determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor whose inner corner is a quarter-circle of radius $\rho$.

title: Carmichael numbers with prime digit sum
words: Show infinitely many Carmichael numbers have a digit sum that is prime.
math: Prove infinitely many Carmichael numbers $n$ with $s_{10}(n)$ prime.

title: Fire on a random tree
words: On a tree where each node has three branches, fire jumps to two random branches per step. Can one firefighter per turn win?
math: On the 3-ary tree with fire spreading to a uniform random 2 of 3 children each step, compute $\Pr(\text{containment})$ with one protection per turn.

title: Sofa with a rotating door
words: A door at the corner swings shut as you move. Find the largest shape that still gets through.
math: Determine the maximal area of a set passing the width-1 right-angled corridor while the region $\{x>1,y>1\}$ moves by a prescribed rotating half-line barrier.

title: Fewest burned cells
words: In the wind-driven fire (spreading only east, north and south), with the fewest firefighters that can trap it, what is the least area that must burn?
math: For the minimal $k$ in the east/north/south fire on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, find $\min |B_\infty|$ over all protection strategies.

title: Nodal domains of the hat drum
words: Count the regions a hat-shaped drum splits into when vibrating at high frequencies.
math: For Dirichlet eigenfunctions on the hat polygon, prove $\limsup N(\varphi_k)/k=c<1$ and compute $c$.

title: Time-independent force
words: Make viscous fluid blow up with a push that never changes in time.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported time-independent $f$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes from rest blows up in finite time.

title: Mod-3 Collatz has no loops beyond the obvious
words: Find every loop of the mod-3 Collatz-like map, and prove there are no others.
math: For $h(n)=n/3,\ 2n+1,\ 2n-1$ (by $n\bmod 3$), determine all periodic orbits in $\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$.

title: Spectre vs hat dimers
words: Show the spectre tiling and the hat tiling have different domino-covering entropies.
math: Prove the dimer entropies per vertex of the spectre and hat adjacency graphs differ.

title: All forests graceful
words: Show every forest with one more vertex than needed can be gracefully labelled.
math: Prove every forest with $m$ edges has an injective labeling into $\{0,\dots,m\}$ with distinct edge differences.

title: Toroidal Sudoku
words: Sudoku where the 3 × 3 boxes wrap around the board's edges. What is the fewest clues for a unique solution?
math: For the $9\times9$ Sudoku variant whose box regions are a fixed partition into wrapped $3\times3$ blocks on $\mathbb{Z}_9^2$, find the minimum number of givens.

title: Hat treewidth
words: Find exactly how hard hat-tiled regions are to break into small pieces.
math: Prove the treewidth of $n$-tile hat patches is $\sim c\sqrt n$ and compute $c$.

title: Hyperbolic sofa
words: Find the largest sofa that can turn a right-angled corner in a hallway of width 1 in the hyperbolic plane, and prove it is best.
math: Determine $\sup\{\operatorname{area}(S)\}$ over sets $S\subset\mathbb{H}^2$ admissible in the width-1 right-angled corridor, and an optimizer.

title: SOF Collatz is undecidable in general
words: Show some natural family of smallest-factor Collatz maps has an undecidable reach-1 question.
math: Prove the problem "given $a,b$, does every orbit of $n\mapsto n/2$ or $\mathrm{spf}(an+b)$ reach 1?" is undecidable.

title: No nice rank 2.5
words: An operation halfway between multiplication and exponentiation cannot be both commutative and associative while varying smoothly with rank.
math: Prove no family $a[s]b$, continuous in $s\in[2,3]$ and matching $\times,\uparrow$ at $s=2,3$, has $a[2.5]b$ commutative and associative on $\mathbb{R}_{>1}$.

title: Grid origami is NP-hard
words: Even when all creases lie on a square grid, deciding flat-foldability with a given layer order should be hard.
math: Prove NP-hardness of flat-foldability (with prescribed mountain–valley assignment) for crease patterns on the square grid with diagonals.

title: Emirp upper bound
words: Primes whose reversal is a different prime should be rarer than primes. Show they thin out like twin primes at most.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: \operatorname{rev}(p)\ne p \text{ prime}\}\ll x/(\log x)^2$.

title: Sofa for every corridor
words: Give one method that finds the best sofa for every hallway shape.
math: Prove optimal sofas for piecewise-linear corridors are characterized by a finite system of ODEs on boundary arcs, and solve it in closed form for all right-angle corridors of width ratio $r$.

title: Pipe-bend sofa
words: A round pipe of diameter 1 bends at a right angle. What is the biggest solid that fits around the bend?
math: Maximize volume over rigid-motion-admissible solids in the union of two half-cylinders of diameter 1 meeting at a right angle.

title: Finite simple groups in Lean
words: Turn the classification of finite simple groups into one computer-checked proof.
math: Formalize the classification of finite simple groups in Lean 4.

title: Spectre dimers are critical
words: Show random pairings of spectre tiles have long-range correlations, like the square grid.
math: Prove dimer correlations on the spectre tiling decay as a power law with exponent 2.

title: Random Sudoku uniqueness
words: Take a random finished Sudoku and keep 25 random cells. How often does that leave exactly one solution?
math: For a uniform random valid grid and a uniform random 25-subset of cells, compute $\Pr(\text{unique completion})$ to three decimals.

title: Prime pancakes
words: Sort pancakes by flipping only a prime number at a time. Find the worst-case number of flips asymptotically.
math: With prefix reversals of prime length, determine $\lim_n d(n)/n$ for the worst-case sorting distance $d(n)$.

title: Prime ladders
words: Change one digit at a time, staying prime. Show any two k-digit primes are linked by at most k + 1 steps.
math: In the graph on $k$-digit primes joined when differing in one decimal digit, prove $\operatorname{diam}\le k+1$ for all $k$.

title: Hyperbolic Hammersley sofa
words: Hammersley built a telephone-shaped sofa that turns a corner. Rebuild it in the hyperbolic plane and compute its area.
math: In $\mathbb{H}^2$ (curvature $-1$) with a width-1 right-angled corridor, adapt Hammersley's construction (two quarter-discs, a block, a removed half-disc) and compute its area.

title: Squared rectangles with prime sides
words: Find the smallest perfect squared rectangle whose squares all have prime side lengths.
math: Determine the minimal order of a perfect squared rectangle with every component side prime.

title: Spectre percolation
words: Show percolation on the spectre tiling and the hat tiling have different thresholds.
math: Prove $p_c^{\text{site}}(\text{spectre})\ne p_c^{\text{site}}(\text{hat})$.

title: Twin-free stretches
words: Find long stretches full of primes but containing no twin primes.
math: Prove there are intervals $[x,x+(\log x)^{1.1}]$ with $\ge(\log x)^{0.05}$ primes but no twin pair, for infinitely many $x$.

title: Random lonely runners
words: With random speeds, runners get noticeably lonelier than the conjecture promises.
math: For i.i.d. uniform speeds in $[1,N]$, $N\gg n^3$, prove the loneliness gap exceeds $\frac1{n+1}+c\frac{\log n}{n^2}$ with probability $\to1$.

title: Graceful star forests
words: Show that any collection of separate star graphs can be labeled so that all edge differences are distinct.
math: For a forest of stars with $m$ edges and $c$ components, find a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+c-1\}$ with distinct edge differences.
